utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T,the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, Counsel Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I should like to inform the Court that the witness Mirko Vidovic is here, and he brought along the originals of the documents mentioned yesterday here. Also, we can say that my learned friend from the Prosecution has had an opportunity to scrutinise these documents before this session, and I should like everybody to look at these documents, and I also wish to tender them as Exhibits D28/3, D29/3, and D30/3. The witness is here, and if need be he can answer any additional questions regarding these documents. Thank you. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We would like to ask the witness to explain the meaning of the stamp on page 19 of his passport "Ausnahme Fur Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland," dated the 24th of September, '92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please, Mr. Vidovic, could you please tell us when this stamp was put on your passport and for which purpose? It was put by the border police.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: When and for which purpose?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a tourist, on the 24th of September, '92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry. As a tourist, were you going to Germany or were you leaving Germany?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Entering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You were entering.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Now, I think I can read here "autobahn." So that means it was the border -- you didn't go by train? Did you go there by train or by car?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: By car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Is so that means that each time you entered Germany you got such a stamp on your passport; is it so?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Why not? Because on other occasions you also went there by car and there was no such stamp.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because he sent my documents to the border in Salzburg that he was taking us in in his name, and to know how it goes from there by fax. I received a message from fax that he was taking us in to his place as a tourist, as far as I can remember. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Vidovic, is this an old passport which you are no longer using?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I did not use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So you can leave it? I mean, I don't know whether Counsel Par is agreeable. Can it be put in evidence, the original passport? Otherwise, we have to take very clear photos of the whole passport.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, Your Honours. All these documents, if necessary. We have to ask the witness whether he will need these documents for anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you need these documents?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So I think all these documents -- not only the passport but all the other papers could also be entered in as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: We received the original documents today. If I may, Your Honours, I should like to ask two questions in order to clarify this German visa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were issued this German visa to enter Germany -- would you look at it -- what period of time were you granted that, three months until the 23rd of December. It says the 24th of September '92 until the 23rd of December, '92.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a multiple entry visa for Germany or was it a single entry visa? I'm referring, of course, to the period of this time.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During this period of time I could come in and go out many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Radovic. Mr. Terrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Allow me to make some observations on this document which I had the time to look at for a couple of minutes before. By all accounts, it seems like it is a visa issued the 24th of September, 1992, valid for three months, but there is a first advertisement or announcement of expulsion of eviction on the first page, and on the following page there is another such indication. So by looking at the document for the first time, it looks as though this witness had been evicted or had been expelled out of the German Republic on two accounts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: There is a stamp on the page before the Ausnahme visa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: It's not the one we have had a look at, it is another one but with different handwriting and no date. So we can wonder whether the witness was not, as a matter of fact, expelled on two occasions out of the German Federal Republic, possibly during the duration -- the valid duration of his passport, because, as you know, anyone can be taken to the border and expelled if there is any violation, if you're working in the black market or for other reasons of the type, and the witness did not conceal the fact that he had worked illegally in Germany. I had another question by looking at that document. We see on several accounts entry visas into Croatia, the border between Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia was crossed on several occasions late in December 1992 and earlier 1993. In March, 1993, the border pass was issued, and some kind of a permanent permit which allows you to cross the border, and that permit is valid for three months. It looks as though the witness was often going to Croatia during that time, and that he even was entitled to have an easy access to that border between Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia. There has been no explanation for it, no explanation coming from his trade or occupation, because he seems to be a worker in a shop or a company for building materials, and that doesn't justify the many journeys he has undertaken, he undertook then. So these are the two questions I had in mind which I wanted to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me, but in relation to the matters raised by my learned friends, I suggest that we immediately ask the witness if we can clarify that. Is it true that he crossed with that card on several occasions? Perhaps we should not make any undue inferences, since the witness is here. Perhaps we could examine him to this fact, and if my learned friend from the Prosecution does not want to do that then perhaps I could ask him some questions regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: What do you mean this letter? You mean this border pass?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes. If I understood my learned friend properly, he said that this card, this border pass, allows one to cross the Croatian-Bosnian border within a three-month period, and he answered yesterday's dilemma, why was the stamp missing from this document, because the stamp is for one crossing and the card is for multiple crossings. The Prosecution then infers that the witness crossed the border many times during the time without any obvious reasons to do so. The Defence claims, on the basis of this card, that he only entered once Croatia to go to Germany and this seems to become a disputable issue. I'm proposing that we examine the witness, whether he used the card only once and then went to Germany, or was he constantly moving to and fro between Bosnia and Croatia. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honours, may I ask two or three questions of this witness to try to clarify this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Well, if you wish. If you insist, yes, but very briefly, because we think that we have the evidence of the witness. As for the exhibits, it is very clear that the only exhibit which is convincing -- well, the only exhibit that proves he was in Germany is the Germany deportation order of the. 29th of July, '93, and that's all. As for his trips to Croatia from Germany in March or April '93, we have only his testimony. But, as I say, if you wish to put questions, do so but very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, I will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirko, please, with this border pass of the 22nd of March, '93, did you go out of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the basis of that, you went to Germany?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether within this period of time between the 22nd of March, '93 until June '95, did you ever come back to Bosnia and use this card?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your entry into Germany only single, only one of the basis of this pass, or did you have several entries into Germany.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is the card to enter once when you come. When you get there you get this card and the date is written there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 1st of June when you entered Germany, did you come out and go in again?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I have no more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I have no questions, but Mr. Par apparently asked the question of the witness, who answered in the affirmative. He asked whether he entered Germany on the basis, on the strength of the border pass, but obviously the border pass doesn't make it possible for Mr. Vidovic to go to Germany but, rather, to Croatia. There seems to be a misunderstanding either in the question or in the answer or in either, but I have no question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. I think we have now sufficiently delved into this matter. If there is no objection, we can release Mr. Vidovic. Mr. Vidovic, thank you for giving evidence. Thank you also for these documents. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I don't know what you decided to admit as Exhibits D28, 29 and 30/3. Were they admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. If there is no objection from the Prosecution we shall admit into evidence the originals. I assume this is Mr. Rajic? (The witness entered court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please introduce yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I am Anto Rajic, born on the 22nd February, '53, in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your place of residence?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: My place of residence is Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please tell us your address?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Santici. No number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please, on this [redacted] air photograph, show us where your house is? I don't know if you can see it here.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, you can't see it here, but this is my brother's house (indicating), and right next to it is mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So somewhere in this lower end?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, are you related to Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, their sister is my wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your part of the village, in Santici, were the majority there Croats, or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The majority were Croats, but there were also some Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Muslim houses were there in that part of the village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, some four or five. Five. Five houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who owned them? Could you give us their names, please?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Serif Ahmic, his brother-in-law, Naho Sabanovic, [redacted] but he has been in Germany for a long time, so I don't know his name. But two sons-in-law, and Serif [redacted] daughter also lived in that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that part of Santici, what were the inter-ethnic relations, or rather relations between Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Oh, well, they were very good. It was mostly young people, with the exception of Serif, who was a man of advanced age. He was 65, 70, something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no problems?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. We even socialised when we were younger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, where did you work then?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In 1992, I worked at Vitezit. That is, it is called Vitezit today. At that time it was called SPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your job?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was a high-skilled metal worker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your military service, did you have your reserve deployment?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time I was assigned to the then anti-aircraft defence, and that is where I was until the end, until 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean -- when you use this acronym, it means anti-aircraft defence; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you mobilised? When were you activated as a member of the AAD?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April, '92, two days after the attack on Sarajevo. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you activated? Why was the anti-aircraft defence activated in that area?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because at that time there was already a danger of aircraft, because of the Serbs. That is, a little later, the Serbs began to bombard, so that we protected the area between the SPS and Impregnacija. They are two companies in Vitez. That is to say above the SPS factory and the Impregnacija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the significance of the possible bombing of the SPS?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was an explosives factory, and of course there was a danger involved, that the entire city would be threatened if it were to be attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is to say that the deployment was around those two factories?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many guns were there on the anti-aircraft defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the anti-aircraft defence there were twelve, 20 millimetres times 10, and eight of the 40s.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about calibres, right, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, in terms of numbers, how many guns were at which particular position?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: By Impregnacija there were five, and around Princip were the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was around Impregnacija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether this was just by Impregnacija, or a bit further away?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was a field about 500 metres away from Impregnacija, not more than that, so in the immediate vicinity, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, was Vitez ever shelled or bombed? Was it ever bombed by the Serb aviation in '92?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, twice. Once in April and once sometime in July or August, somewhere around then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, where was the anti-aircraft defence first, within which military structure?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The anti-aircraft defence was within the TO, the Territorial Defence. I didn't understand you well. Yes, it was the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have TO insignia?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, for about two months, and then we had PZO insignia. That was anti-aircraft defence. The Muslims had TO, and then -- well, nothing was obligatory, really, because it was a joint thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the Serb ones. While we were TO, we had the olive grey uniforms, all the way up to June or July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are JNA uniforms; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in the PZO, in the anti-aircraft defence, did you also have Muslims with you? You mentioned that they kept TO insignia?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from the very outset, even before we were mobilised, they were in this PZO, or PVO; that is to say the anti-aircraft defence. Yes, there were Muslims there, and that's the way it remained all the way up to October. We were together, the composition was mixed, and we had two shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hold these positions together?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who your commander at that time was?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember his name. He worked in the municipality, but he was there for a very short period of time, but then they changed something up there, the municipality. I can't remember his name. I simply cannot. I tried, but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim, or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: A Muslim. A Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what did you do on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of October I was at home, because my shift was off that day, and in the evening at 10.00 there was an alert -- not really an alert, but we were asked to go to man the guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking about the 9th, or are you talking about the 10th -- are you talking about the 19th of October, or are you talking about the 20th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm talking about the 19th of October, in the evening, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: We went to the positions. There was some kind of an alert. Nothing really happened, and then we went home, and then there was the regular shift at 6.00 in the morning, or a bit before that, actually, because again there was danger of air strikes, so then we had to be there before dawn. I was at the position at about 10 minutes to 6.00 or 15 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which position were you at exactly? This regular position of yours by Impregnacija?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you were there on the 20th of October at quarter to 6.00; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any information about the anti-aircraft defence, whether you had to engage in combat action? Did you receive such orders?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, no. It was only -- there was nothing at the time when he arrived, but then at 6.00 -- yes, around 6.00 in the morning, again there was a state of alert, and then the shooting started in [redacted], but we didn't receive any orders for combat action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard shooting near Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position that you held in the field by Impregnacija, how far away is it from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, about a kilometre and a half, about 1.500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a position to take combat action against Ahmici at all?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, not from that position. No, that position was lower than Ahmici. There is a small hill between us and Ahmici. We couldn't even see Ahmici from there. We could only see the upper part of Pirici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was physically impossible for you to operate from that position?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was simply impossible to see anything from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Midhat Berbic from Ahmici in the PZO in the anti-aircraft defence?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from the very outset, even before that, yes, we were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he with you at that position on the 20th of October, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, he was at a different position. He was at a different position that was by the SPS factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Muslims go into combat action against you? Were they shooting against your positions?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, not in those positions where the guns were. There is Sivrino Selo village which is above those positions so there was no shooting whatsoever not using a gun, not using a rifle, nothing that day. So we were there, on the ready, but no, there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any artillery attacks vis-à-vis Ahmici that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where from, from which position?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: From the position of Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Hrasno. Somebody calls it Hrasno and other people call it Rasno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which municipality? Which municipality does Hrasno belong to?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's municipality of Busovaca. Across the Lasva River, that's where the Busovaca municipality is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was operating on the territory of the Busovaca municipality? Who had military control over it? The HVO of Vitez or the HVO of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Naturally the HVO of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us on this aerial image, perhaps, we can move this top one away and show you the other one, can you show us your positions around the Lasva River Valley and where Hrasno was?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So could the usher please remove this aerial photograph of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you have to stand so that the Judges can see you too.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Just by the road, here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by the road, that is where Impregnacija is?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the field where you were positioned; right? And where is Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Hrasno is here (indicating). Here. Can you hear me? We could not see this area where the gun was at Hrasno, we couldn't see it from our position. So the gun at Hrasno was basically concealed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you knew that this artillery attack came from there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a small distance. If it's 1.500 metres to Ahmici, in this direction it could be about 2.000 metres. So you can hear artillery and you can also recognise the three-barrel gun when it shoots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Did the Muslims have some kind of artillery pieces in Sivrino Selo?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any information, but we had heard they had a recoilless gun and that there was danger from there because from our positions Sivrino Selo was only about 500 metres away, even less than that. So this was a danger for our guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sivrino Selo was Muslim, entirely Muslim; wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened with the PZO after the conflict on the 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Then the PZO was divided. It was literally divided, split up. The cannons were split up between the Muslims and the Croats. We or, rather, not we, the group from the upper position by Princip took two guns and two guns were taken, I don't know where, but they were taken to the Muslim side, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who took these guns away to the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Midhat Berbic. He was the commander and he took it over. It was a group. It was a simple split-up. Two guns went this side, and two guns they took for themselves, and Midhat Berbic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the commander of this position by Princip; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and it is from that position that these two guns were taken away, whereas the remaining four stayed with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know the reasons for the conflict on the 20th of October, 1992? Do you know why a conflict took place?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The road between Busovaca-Travnik-Jajce was blocked. The Muslims from Ahmici blocked the road by Topolsko cemetery, and that is when the shooting started because the Busovaca and the Kiseljak units were supposed to go to Novi Travnik, or rather, to Jajce. Jajce was about to fall at that time. Because of these tensions, they could not pass because of the Muslims and that is when this serious conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was killed on the Croatian side during this conflict and where that person was from?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know his last name. His last name is Vidovic. He's from Kiseljak, and he was killed. On the Muslim side Pezer was killed, and I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Croats from the village took part in the conflict in Ahmici on the 20th of October in any way?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. No, the Croats from Ahmici, Santici, and Pirici did not take part in this. It was simply a blockade that was carried out by the Muslims, and the units from Kiseljak and Busovaca took part in this conflict on the other site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is important is that you did not have any orders to take action, although your permanent position was there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was our permanent position. We were on the ready, and then the three-barrel gun at Hrasno was operated, but we couldn't see it so we did not take any action all day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you hear shooting that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Until sometime in the afternoon. I don't know exactly what time it was. It was scarcer and scarcer and then it finally stopped in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were your shifts organised? How much time would you spend manning a gun? How much time would you spend there and how much time would you spend at home?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, we would be on duty for three days and then we would spend three days at home, but we would always leave a guard overnight around the guns so that we could get some rest, because we would have to be there all day, and there were alerts because of planes and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you go home on the 20th, in the evening?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you find there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I found my wife's family there. That is to say, Mira Kupreskic, Zoran's wife, with three children; and Ljuba Kupreskic with two children; and also my mother-in-law, that is to say, my wife's mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they at your place then?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: There was a danger. They were in the upper part of Ahmici or, rather, Pirici, and no one knew exactly what was going on, at least they didn't know, the civilians, and they didn't want the gun from Hrasno to hit them or a bullet or something. So then they fled to my house because there was no shooting up there, no. It was quite peaceful and quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did they stay at your place?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Four or five days, because I went out to the position again, and then I'd just come back home and get some rest. Four or five days, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why they stayed that long? Because you said that on the next day or, rather, that day, in the afternoon, there was no more shooting.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the Muslim part didn't go back immediately either. People were afraid. They didn't know whether that would be it, whether it was just this first day or whether this would continue. So they simply felt safer. They wanted to be safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the Muslims returned, and did the Muslims from your part of the village flee?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: You mean during that conflict?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The first conflict.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. They stayed in the village all the time. They were not threatened in any way. We did not threaten them in any way so they stayed throughout, although, they were probably afraid, just like we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Muslims from the rest of Santici, Pirici, Ahmici escaped?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Muslims from the rest of the village and from the rest of Ahmici, Santici, Pirici, whether they had fled too?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. That first day everybody fled. That I know, naturally. Then after a few days, the older people started returning, and they said, "Well, we have nothing to do with this," and they returned to the village. The younger ones started coming back a bit later, when things were completely peaceful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that the younger people came back later? Did you see that? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that and I saw it. I think they took part in the blockade of this part, and they were probably afraid. I mean, they were afraid that something might happen to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know whether some meetings were held in the village after this first conflict?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, meetings were held in the school in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take part in this?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, but my father did, so I'm aware of that. I've received information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the point of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The point of these meetings was to reduce the tensions that were there on the eve of the 20th and on the 20th, and mostly it was elderly people. It was at their initiative, but there was also younger people who took part in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, in your part of the village, were there any guards, village guards?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, they were not organised but they existed, again at people's own initiative, because in my village, quite a number of us were in the anti-aircraft defence. Fifty per cent of them were able-bodied men, and then there were elderly mean of 50 or 60 years of age, and they simply, because we were away, they organised it. Well, not guards but patrols, because if you are a guard you stand in one place and a patrol goes around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make part of the village guards?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Because I was assigned with the anti-aircraft defence, so I was on the positions all day, and the rest of it I used to have some rest, with the help of my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So people who were assigned to some military duty did not go on guarding duty; is that it?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, where did you go? Where did you relocate after the conflict of the 20th of October, '92, and after the Croats and Muslims in the anti-aircraft defence separated?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: We stayed for another three days at that position and then we relocated to Gornja Rovna. It's next to Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I think you could indicate its location to us. Where is Gornja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Gornja Rovna is here, I think (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Oh, until late November. It could have been the 27th or the 28th. There we also had shifts, three-day-shifts. For the first two days we were there all the time because, of course, the tension was high, and then we realised that nothing was happening, and then we took three-day-shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that position?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: After that position, with my gun I went to a locality Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please indicate where Prahulje is?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, it's not here. No, because it is in the municipality of Travnik. So it is four kilometres away from Travnik. That is at a distance of some 14 kilometres from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it -- perhaps you --

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Bila here, Nova Bila?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Bila you're asking? (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So Prahulje is even further down?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Further down towards Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please take your seat again? It was in the municipality of Novi Travnik; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Travnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you made part of what units?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that is where we were relocated, because we then acted within the Novi Travnik Brigade, Petar Tomasevic or Stjepan Tomasevic. I can't remember exactly what it was called. Stjepan Tomasevic. We did not act, we simply deployed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your function there, that is, at Prahulje? What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: We guarded the howitzer, 122 millimetres, because on Vlasic, on the hill, we could often see helicopters. The howitzer, without that gun, we would be quite unprotected. This AAD gun was supposed to protect the area so that it would not be shelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were there to provide defence against Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Quite so, yes, because in the municipality of Travnik, there was no sign of a mounting tension or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the howitzer was then at a position held by the Croat army, facing the Serbs; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was there to protect that gun?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Mirko Safradin, Goran Vuleta were on my shift, Marko Grgic. So the four of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, were you there on the 16th of April, '93 when the war in the Lasva Valley broke out?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I was right there at that position at Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to what was going on in a different part of the Vitez municipality? Did you have any communication with Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: We had communication with Novi Travnik but, of course, we had the radio station and around to -- well, we could, of course, communicate with Vitez at a different frequency, of course. I tried to get some information, and I learned that in Ahmici, the village of Ahmici, there was shooting and then the village was on fire, but they still didn't know what was going on. I was surprised, and I tried to establish the connection once again, but then I could not because the communication was disrupted, was cut off, and for the next two days I could establish no communication until I was relocated to yet another position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you could not get the radio -- you could not communicate by radio; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, by radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you could not communicate with Vitez by radio but you could with Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, we could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did they have any information?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. No, they did not have any information as to what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other contact with your home or anything? Did you know what was going on in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That evening I tried to get home. I tried to communicate with my home. I called my wife, and she told me that there was shooting, the village was on fire, but they didn't know what was going on, indeed, either, and they moved to a shelter that night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What night do you mean that they went to a shelter?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The first night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was what, the day of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. The night, the 16th. In the evening of the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, in your part of the village you say that you had Muslim neighbours there. Was any one of those Muslims killed?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In my part? No. Of those five houses, well, one of them -- one from those five houses was in Germany with his wife, but the others are all alive and they were even all with us. I mean, not with us, but with the wife in the basement. That is what she told me when I came home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Muslims from your part of the village were hiding in the basement with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the first night, because they were also at a loss what was happening. In that part there was no shooting. They saw that that is where they sought refuge. They knew that it was -- that Ahmici -- I'm not too sure, there because they were local people, so -- but they came there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Croats capture them after that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. Instead, they took them under custody -- I mean, transferred them from Sivrino Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the army or did the neighbours help them to get out?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Both the neighbours and a part of the army, because they were mostly elderly people. Of course, elderly people are always more frightened. They were also our army, our men who then transferred them, took them to the other side -- to their side, the Muslim one. There is a road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was when?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: It was on the 17th, in the morning of the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sivrino Selo is a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is a purely Muslim village. Except there is a part -- it is not called Sivrino Selo, even though it was made part of it, and that was -- that had Croat inhabitants and it is a locality called Kremenjace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sivrino Selo is very near Santici, is that so, the part of Santici that you live in?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Correct. It is so near that I can recognise a man. I can recognise a man in Sivrino village it's so close. It's 300 metres from the end of my village to theirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So will you please, on this big aerial photograph, indicate where Sivrino Selo is in relation to Santici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: This is the locality of Kremenjace, this part here, and this here is Sivrino Selo (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is this lower part of Santici where your house is?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: (indicating)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In view of the small distance, do you know, or perhaps did your wife tell you if there were any combat actions taken by Croats against Sivrino Selo on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 16th, no. There was more shooting there -- well, Ahmici is near, but from Sivrino Selo in the direction of Santici, there was no action on the first day, that is, on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You may take your seat again. Will you tell us, please, if you know Mirjan Santic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Mirjan Santic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Oh, well, he was a relative of mine, and he was with me on the anti-aircraft defence, but on another shift. He perished towards the end of January or early February -- he moved from -- in the end of January or beginning of February, and then he went to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His house in Santici was near your house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, some 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when he was killed and where?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, '93, in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you positive?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of what unit?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: As a member of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Slavko Sakic?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I do. Yes. And I know that he was also on the anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that exactly, because I was at Pramulje, so that I really have no idea where they were. I didn't even know where my wife and children were, let alone others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, do you know who the Jokers were?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was military police, a part of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were accommodated?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were near Nadioci, at the Bungalow, that is what it was called, a kind of a motel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of uniforms they had? Did you ever see them?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I saw them. They had black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, did you ever learn who took part in the conflict in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I know for certain that it was the military police, because Mirjan was a relative of mine and also a colleague, and I also heard the Jokers participated in it, too. I could not see that, because ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell us, you remained at your position at Pramulje, or did you move?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I stayed at Pramulje because Mirko arrived on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mirko who?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Mirko Safradin, because he was free at the time, he was on my shift -- no, I mean there were four of us, and since it was quiet, we would always leave one of us to have a rest. So he was to come to replace me on the 16th, but of course he could not. So we stayed there, Goran Vuleta and I were there alone on the 16th, and on the 17th, Mirko came to me in the morning or so, and we were there until the morning of the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: On the 18th, the orders came from the Novi Travnik Brigade to relocate to Pokrajcici, and that is a locality in the Travnik municipality above Zabilje. That is a hill, an elevation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see that on this map?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see Zabilje here, right at the end. Should I stand up? Here's the village of Zabilje (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is this hill?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The hill is over here. So we're here, across from this (indicating). This is where the hill is, and this is the place where we were positioned. A bit lower than this, actually, but here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What municipality is that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: That is the municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you transferred -- please take a seat; thank you. Why were you transferred to that position on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, on the 17th of the evening, this position of Brdo, this hill, fell. That's where our people were, the anti-aircraft people. They had the Strelas, and they were attacked on the 17th, in the evening, and this position was taken, and then our people withdrew to the village of Zabilje, and they established a line there, and they tried to recapture Brdo, because it's very important, and the entire village was immediately threatened. So that is why we were sent there as support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 17th, Brdo was taken by the BH army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the 17th, in the evening, during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you were transferred there, and what did you do? Was there shooting there, around Zabilje, on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: As we were being transferred -- all of this is nearby, and you can hear rifles and guns. Yes, there was shooting, and when we arrived at the position -- that was around noon, I think -- the shooting was abating. So we positioned ourselves, but the shooting stopped, and we did not take any action that day at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, we were preparing the position. We didn't have any accommodation, we didn't have any food. All of this was done in haste. So I went to the village, and night had already started to fall, because it takes time to prepare a position. So this was dusk, when we went to see where we could spend the night and where we could eat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: We went to the village, to Jaka Bilic. I didn't know her name at the time. This woman invited us to spend the night at her place, and she said, "If you didn't have any place to sleep, you could stay here," she said. Mirko Safradin, Goran Vuleta, and I stopped there, and we had dinner. We had dinner around 7.00, 6.30 or 7.00. Then we had a cup of coffee, naturally, and we watched the news on television. We wanted to hear information as to what was going on. I wish to note once again that I had lost all contact with my family. I didn't know where my wife was and where my children were during those three days, that is to say, from the 16th in the evening until the 18th, I didn't know a thing, and all sorts of stories were going about, that people had fled to Busovaca, and then they said "No, now they're at home," and "Now they're in Kiseljak." So this information was harrowing, and I was wondering whether I could get any proper information on the TV news.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were very interested in what you could hear concerning all the news from that area?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall which TV news you watched that night?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In the evening, yes, I watched the Bosnian news, TV Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, TV Sarajevo. In this municipality of Travnik, because you were in the municipality of Travnik at the time, and this TV news program from Sarajevo was broadcast --

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. There were no conflicts, and there was electricity, so we watched those TV news during the remaining few days while we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell me what you saw in this TV news? What was in the headlines that day?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The village of Ahmici was in the headlines, the conflict in Ahmici. It is probably CNN and other foreign TV news programs and crews that had filmed this, because I don't think Bosnian TV could have done it at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was shown on TV? What did you see from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, at first we saw houses on fire, smoke, houses on fire. All this was -- this was taken from afar; it wasn't really close up. Then there were a few corpses down by this place called Sangaj. I recognised it because I'm from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean by the cafe of Sangaj?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the parking lot by the cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's on the road by the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Then there was some footage from the Zenica hospital. I followed all the news very carefully to see what would happen, and I watched this very carefully to see whether I could recognise someone, because I knew a lot of Muslims from Ahmici, and perhaps I could hear some information as to what happened to Ahmici and Santici. Then I saw a man. I didn't even know who he was. He introduced himself. He said his name was [redacted]. I knew a [redacted] who lived at the bottom of the village, but I saw it wasn't that [redacted] [redacted], so I was wondering what he would say and what had happened to him and what happened to the rest and what happened to Zoran and Mica and my mother-in-law and their mother and my father-in-law. All of this is nearby. I wanted to know what had happened to all of them, whether they were alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see? What did this man look like?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: This man had his hands and arms burned all the way up to the elbows. He was sort of sitting in bed, half reclining, half sitting. His hair was dishevelled. His face was a bit burned, too, and then he talked about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say? What had happened?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: He said that soldiers burst into the village and that they torched the village and that two soldiers barged into his house and that they were masked -- or rather that they were painted, they had paint on their faces, and that they killed his son, his daughter-in-law, and a three-month-old child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when he said all of that, did the reporter ask him any questions?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The reporter insisted, said, "Did you know who did this?" And he said, "No, no, I couldn't recognise anyone." I was also very interested in hearing this. So he was asked twice, and I was also interested in hearing whether he would say who did this, but persistently he kept saying then that he didn't know who did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say why he did not recognise these men? How come he did not recognise them? Did he give a reason?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he gave a reason. He said that they were masked, in the sense of their faces being painted, and naturally it was impossible for him to recognise them. He just said that they had black clothing. He didn't name anyone in that report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that you didn't know who this [redacted] was. When did you find out which [redacted] this was?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I found out only in 1997. People tried to explain this to me, what this [redacted] looked like, I mean, after all of that, but I could not remember who he was. My wife even said, "Oh, come on, how come you can't remember? He was a driver in Impregnacija." I simply could not remember. I kept thinking of this other [redacted] who lived in the lower part of the village. It's only in 1997, when this [redacted]

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: was on television. She watches television on Mondays, and TV Travnik also shows this series, it's called The Hague Diary, and they probably get footage only that they can find, you see. So she told me that she saw [redacted]. She said, "Why don't you watch this on Thursday, too, and perhaps you'll recognise him, you'll know who this [redacted] is."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were supposed to see a replay of the show; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a replay. I watched this replay on Thursday, and as I watched him on television, I said "Well, that was the man who was in the hospital that time, this same [redacted]." She said, "Is that that [redacted]?" And I said "Yes, yes, that's the one I saw who was at the Zenica hospital at the time." But even before that, he had accused Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic. I heard about that on Radio Zenica, and I read about it in the papers, too, and I said, "I know, 100 per cent sure, I'm 100 per cent sure that in that TV news programme, he had said that he had not recognised anyone." Then, when I realised that it was the same person, then I realised that I would come here as a witness too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The statement that we gave to the Court, translated, is it true what is said here, that you gave it to us on the 27th of February, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that cassette before that? So what is contained here in this statement, is it only your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is only my recollection. I tried to find this cassette on my own, because I thought that it had to be recorded somewhere. No, no, all the way up to Germany. We simply could not find it. So this is my recollection only; how I remember this, what he looked like, what he said. Whether I memorised every little word he said, I don't know. I mean, maybe he said something else too. But what I know for sure, 100 per cent, is that he said that he did not recognise anyone. I was really interested in what was going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We could not find that cassette, but then after filing your statement, we received a cassette from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could we now see P157, Prosecutor's Exhibit 157.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say what is missing from this statement? Is that everything that you heard on that day? (Videotape played) THE INTERPRETER (Voiceover): On the 16th of April, sometime in the morning, we were asleep. The child was crying. I had a grandson who was three months old, three months and three days on this day. My son turned on the light, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Part of it is inaudible. THE INTERPRETER (Voiceover): -- and I was asleep over there. In the meantime, these men from HOS -- no, the HVO soldiers, they came, they barged through the door, they broke the door open, and they fired a burst of gunfire at the veranda. They got into the room. The light was on. They saw my son, he was on his feet, and they killed him straight away. I was peeking through the door that I only kept ajar. Then they shot bursts of gunfire into my daughter-in-law and my other grandson. However, the child that was in the cradle made some noise, and then this man came back and shot a burst of gunfire into the baby who was in the cradle, that was three months and three days old. They got out. They left. They immediately created two fires in the kitchen downstairs. The flames spread very quickly, and I tried to get the children into this room where I was, so that I could localise it as much as possible. These children had been killed, but I didn't want them to burn, too. However, I didn't manage to do a thing. The flames were very quick. I was sitting in this room, and the outside window was open, and this other room where the children were asleep, there the door and the window had burned down already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you've seen the recording that we have. Is anything missing there? Was this the end?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, the end is missing. This last statement that he made, when the reporter asked him -- I can't remember whether it was man or a woman reporter -- the reporter said, "Did you recognise these people? Try to remember." And he said, "No, I couldn't, because they were masked." That's exactly what he said. That part has been cut off from this cassette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that have been the logical question to ask, too?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, quite logical. I mean, if they are seeking information, if you know what happened, let's see who did it. It's logical for a journalist to ask that kind of question, and that's why I know that the journalist had put this question, and I was expecting him to name someone, but he didn't name anyone. He said just what I told you here; "I didn't recognise them because they were masked. They had paint on their faces."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, at that time in Zenica on the 17th and 18th, were there any war operations? Was there any fighting in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In Zenica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell because I was not up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose control was Zenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Under Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the way things remained; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have concluded and it is time for the break now; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. I assume there will be no cross-examination by other Defence counsel, so we'll take a break and then we'll move to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Terrier:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajic. I'm Franck Terrier, one of the Prosecutors, and I intend to ask a couple of questions following the examination-in-chief. You said that there is a -- you're a relative with Mirjan and Zoran Kupreskic, that somehow they are your brothers-in-law. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. I'm their brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We got that. Is there an addition to this link, the family link? Did you also have friendship links with them? Were you befriended with them?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We knew one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen that you and your wife paid regular visits to them? I'm talking about 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, whenever we could. Yes. In '92, yes. In '93 not so often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know their neighbours in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: You mean Muslims. Well, I did know some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- make no difference between Muslims and Croats, I'm just asking you whether you knew their neighbours.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, particularly younger people, those of my age, more or less. I knew less of those who were older.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to name some of the neighbours, some of Mirjan's and Zoran's neighbours at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Sukrija Ahmic, [redacted], down there, the one by the road. Nermin Ahmic, likewise. He's more or less my age. Enisa Ahmic, and others. I can't recall their names right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You no longer remember them. I see. Let us, for a while, speak of the responsibilities that were yours in terms of anti-aircraft defence. If I remember well, you said that you were mobilised in April 1992 in order to ensure the anti-aircraft protection of Impregnacija, the Impregnacija buildings; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your own responsibilities in that field?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was the leader, the commander, for one gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the type, the model, the calibre? Yes, the type of cannon it was.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is Bufors 40-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this 40-millimetre calibre was manned by how many people?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: According to regulation, there should be five and the driver. That is the sixth one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a self-propelled cannon? It was mounted on a vehicle; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No, it had wheels but then it was attached to a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to remind us of the time when you left that position, that Impregnacija position, together with a gun?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was on the 18th -- no, on the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 23rd of October. To which position did you then go?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I went to Gornja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the military tactical reason for that move?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, it was still the anti-aircraft defence, because the tension of the first conflict has come down and yet there was a danger that the conflict might spread or, rather, if it broke out again that then this gun could be destroyed from Sivrino Selo, and that was the main reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you move to yet another position? When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that was towards the end of November. Whether it was the 27th or 28th, somewhere there, of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, late November 1992. You probably said so earlier on. I'm sorry for that. But would you mind reminding us of the position you were then supposed to have and take?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: You mean, where I was relocated?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. Well, with the gun.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were relocated from Gornja Rovna to Prahulje municipality of Travnik. Old Travnik, I think, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let us speak about that position. What was your mission? What was your task? What were the instructions you had received?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was put under the command of Novi Travnik. That is a different regiment. We were to protect the 122-millimetre howitzer from helicopters or aircraft as rockets could still be launched from Vlasicici or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your task was to ensure protection of the 122 howitzer ; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, am I wrong in saying that at the time, on the Serbian side -- on the Bosnian Serb side, there is no longer any aircraft power, be it helicopters, combat aircraft, or there is no longer any threat coming from the Serbs at that time; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: That is not true. There was the no-fly orders for Serb aircraft, but Vlasic -- around Vlasic plateau there were helicopters. Aircraft were not allowed to, but helicopters transporting something, I don't know, and there could also be fighter craft.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I then again wrong in saying that the anti-aircraft guns, at the time, were used not to defend that air space that was empty but was aimed at ground objectives and, more specifically so, at houses? Am I wrong in saying that the anti-aircraft gun would send a projectile which has a very large penetrating power and which could cause major damage on houses, could, for instance, torch a house?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: The place where we were at in Prahulje was a depression next to the howitzer and it was impossible to fire at any house. This is all purely Croat space and around there there are hills, hillocks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's speak about that 122-millimetre howitzer in the vicinity of which you were. Was it used at that time? I mean, April 1993, was it used at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In '93, April. No, no. It was used in January '93 too, but it was all aimed at Vlasic plateau.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Zenica was bombed on the 29th of April and that the shells, according to the investigations carried out then, seemed to come from a 122 gun?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I was separated from the howitzer on the 18th of April and relocated to a different position. This howitzer went somewhere. I don't know where. So that is possible, but I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the reach of a 122 gun, in kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly. I was with the anti-aircraft defence, so I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have the slightest idea, sort of an approximate idea of the distance it can cover?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, my guess is from Prahulje it fired at Vlasic plateau. It is 20 or 18 kilometres, so it could be that, perhaps a little more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you mentioned this earlier on, but you said that you left that position on the 18th of April, 1993. Would you be in a position to give us further details on that, when, what time, on whose instructions or orders, and to go where?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: In the morning of the 18th, we left the position at Prahulje, and the orders from Novi Travnik, because that is where the command for the anti-aircraft defence was at the time, and relocated to a locality, to a place called Pokrajcici. That is four kilometres to the south of Prahulje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many kilometres away from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Prahulje, Vitez, it is about 14 kilometres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your objectives at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: When I was relocated to Pokrajcici, it was when a hill fell. It was a very important elevated point because the village of Zabilje was below that. My duty was to support -- that the Muslim units or the BH army does not break through to the village of Zabilje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as I was saying previously, we are no longer talking about anti-aircraft defence. We are mentioning now ground objectives.

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, true. As of the 18th, yes, that is quite true, we worked -- we turned on the ground objectives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No. Yes. Well, within the HVO, but we were in the anti-aircraft defence unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your military rank?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: At that time I still had the old one, that is, the old rank, the rank of the former army, and that was Corporal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you be so kind as to repeat the rank, for the sake of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a Corporal in the Yugoslav army. It was a Lance Corporal, Corporal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take an oath, an oath of allegiance or faith for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know other HVO soldiers who they -- who would have taken that oath, that allegiance oath?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that some of them took it, but I don't know too. The AAD, the anti-aircraft defence, was before that mobilised, and only afterwards the HVO units took the oath of allegiance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you can remember, or as far as you know, when did HVO soldiers start taking that oath?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say when. I could not say exactly or even approximately when. I think it would be a gross error on my part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any such ceremony, oath-taking ceremonies?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, you said earlier on that on the 16th of April, 1993, you heard over the radio that Ahmici was burning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Over the radio station, RUP 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us further specification as to this RUP 12?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, RUP 12 is a radio station. I think it's about half a metre tall and about 30 metres wide, and you can choose frequencies within a 12-to-15-kilometre range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please enlighten me. Are we talking about some military means of communication which would be reserved to military?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, RUP 12 was of the Yugoslav army, and it belonged to us as an AAD unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would be sending information? Who did you hear talking about Ahmici in flames, in fire?

utterances.speaker: ANTO RAJIC
