utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say they were friends of yours, or good acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: They were friends, good acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it that you became aware of the allegation against them implicating them in the alleged incidents in the [redacted] household that [redacted] spoke about?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I learned it in the village. The story spread. People talked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at a subsequent time discuss this position at all with Mr. Rajic, your friend?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes. Afterwards, he asked me -- when we watched that recording, he had seen it once again, and so he asked me if I had done the same, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you have such a conversation with Mr. Rajic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I was with him when he watched it afterwards, a recording of a kind, and then he asked me, but I don't really remember when it was exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that last reply has confused me a little. Are you saying that on some subsequent occasion to the 18th of April, 1993, Mr. Rajic watched a recording again, and you were with him when that happened? Is that what you're saying, sir? I want to be clear on the record.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No, I did not watch it with him. He watched it. Afterwards, once again, he once again watched that recording, and after that he asked me if I had seen it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequent to that conversation, has there ever been a further conversation between you and Mr. Rajic in connection with that video recording, that television interview?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But since that conversation, it is since then that you met with the lawyers for the Kupreskic brothers, and you then gave them a statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you, sir, happen to know a gentleman by the name of Mr. Slavko Sakic?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me who he is and what he does, or what he did at that time, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: What he did at the time, I don't know. He was also a member of the anti-aircraft defence, but what he did, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, as a local from Santici, did you know Mr. Mirjan Santic from that same village?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of Mr. Mirjan Santic's military position in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: All I know is that he was there, on the spot. I don't know what he did, whether he went to conquer, to take something, take possession of something, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you, sir, that Mr. Mirjan Santic was a member of the military police, even of the unit called the Jokers, would that ring any bell with you? Would that provoke a recollection, or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I know that he was a military policeman, but the rest of it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you ever seen him around in any form of uniform in Santici before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for answering my questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'm obliged to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Radovic, do you think we can get through today, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. Yes. Re-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told us how Anto Rajic saw again the programme with [redacted], could you tell us, how could he see the same programme twice on television?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Well, when he watched it twice -- for the second time, it was on that Hague Diary, and I know we talked about it that his wife -- that his wife had watched it on The Hague Diary, and she told him there was a replay on the Thursday or something like that, and he saw it then, and then he recognised it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but tell us, that Hague Diary, did it show old footage or testimony at The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I did not see it. He told me that he had seen what we had seen before, that is, on the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if [redacted] [redacted] Have you ever heard of that?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted] transmitted by the Bosnia and Herzegovina television on its Hague Diary programme?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: All I heard was that Anto had seen it on The Hague Diary. I know nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know exactly what was shown in The Hague Diary?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: He told me that they had shown the same thing that we had seen on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that how you understood him?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what The Hague Diaries feature? Have you ever seen a story on The Hague Diary?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No, I have never seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has anyone ever told you what The Hague Diary was about?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No, only Anto -- except Anto.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I've heard about Anto. You don't have to repeat it five times. But the Prosecution asked you about Mirjan Santic. I did not quite get this question, even though I believe I am quite familiar with the Croatian language, but you were asked whether you knew if Mirjan Santic was a member of the military police. You gave an answer that I really could not fathom out. Did you know that Mirjan Santic was among the military police, or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: First the gentleman did not ask me properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, you did not answer properly, so let us redress that, and I'm asking you if Mirjan Santic was a member of the military police or not.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I know that he was a member of the military police, but where he was and where he went, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody asked you that. All you were asked by the Prosecution was if he was a member of the military police. They never asked you where he went or what he did. Then you also said that you went to your brother's because he was also a member of the gun team, and that you went to fetch him to Novi Travnik. So on your way back from your brother, did he come along? Did your brother come along, or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What had you agreed with him regarding this?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Well, he had to stay over there because he lived in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you know the first and last name of the person that you spent the night of the 18th of April, and where you watched this TV programme that you told us about today? I mean, the name and the address?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Jako Bilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the address?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I only know it was in Pokrajcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know the number of the house?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the area code?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I think it was Travnik, municipality of Travnik. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more thing: As regards your gun, what else belonged to the gun, except for the gun itself? Did you have any communications device?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a radio?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a radio?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: What's it called -- the RUP 12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't handle this radio, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions, and I believe that I did not overstep our regular working hours for too long. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I'm afraid I have one or two questions, however, if you don't mind, since you took three or four minutes. Let me see whether I can, in one or two minutes, ask a few questions of the witness. First of all, Mr. Safradin, did you ever belong to the HVO, either in '92 or '93 or between '92 and '93? Because I didn't understand your answer to the Prosecutor very well.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But still, in your statement, you stated and you signed -- you stated, and I quote your words: "I was a member of the HVO unit of June '92." Probably you meant "since June'92." How do you explain this contradiction? Leaving aside the HVO, when you were there in charge of this gun, which was the military unit to which you belonged? There was some sort of military unit or military hierarchy to which -- organisation to which you belonged; which was this one?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: In June 1992, there was no HVO at all. At that time it was a Territorial Defence unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And then in April '93? At that stage, did you belong to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, you said that you saw this TV programme on the 18th of April. How do you explain now, or how did you explain at that stage, on the 18th of April, that [redacted], as we saw a few minutes ago, in explaining what happened in Ahmici on the 16th of April, said "yesterday," so my inference would be that therefore this broadcast was made on the 17th of April. It started off by saying "yesterday." This is what we got in the English translation. Meaning -- sorry, Mr. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, it did not have to be broadcast on television the very same day when the journalist interviewed him. That would be an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Thank you. But that means that the shooting was done on the 17th, therefore. Now, my last question is about the 16th of April. So you said you spent the whole day at home in Santici while a lot of shooting and shelling was going on nearby, at about one kilometre. How did you spend the whole day? Doing what, at home?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: I didn't do anything. I was simply at home, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But look, you were a military man, and you were not curious about what was happening nearby? People shooting, you heard a lot of shelling and shooting, and you stayed at home without asking yourself about what was happening nearby? I'm just asking what you decided to do, why you just simply stayed at home -- doing what? Reading?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAFRADIN
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know what was going on, but I was a member of the anti-aircraft defence, and I had to be there so that I could receive some information, and I didn't want to go back to the position in Prahulje before I had to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right, I see that my colleagues don't have any questions for you. Thank you, Mr. Safradin, for giving evidence. You may now be released. And we adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
